en.name: Cumin, ground
en.summary: Ground cumin keeps 3–4 years from purchase in a cool, dark cupboard, opened or unopened. An eighteen-month-old jar of cumin is not dangerous — it is just weaker than it was. The figure is a flavour window, not a safety limit.
en.pantry: 3–4 years from purchase in an airtight jar, cool, dark and away from the steam of the hob. Dried, ground cumin has far too little water in it for anything to grow, so nothing is spoiling; the aromatic oils are simply leaving, a little faster in warmth and light. Judge it by smell rather than by date: tip a little into your palm, warm it with your thumb and smell. Fresh cumin is immediate and earthy; a faded jar smells of dust. Whole seed keeps its aroma longer than powder, and a minute in a dry pan before grinding makes even average cumin taste like something.
en.fridge: The fridge is a poor choice for ground cumin. Ground spices are hygroscopic, so each time a cold jar is opened in a warm kitchen, condensation lands on the powder; damp cumin cakes and can mould. A sealed jar in a cupboard away from the cooker is where it wants to be.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published either, and the condensation problem is worse still in the freezer. The genuinely useful move is to buy whole cumin seed, which outlasts the ground spice because less surface is exposed to air, and toast and grind it as you cook. That gives you more than any cold storage could.
en.thawing: Not applicable — ground cumin is a dry cupboard spice and should not be frozen.
spoilage: No smell at all when you warm a pinch in your palm.
A dusty, flat aroma instead of a warm, earthy one.
Caking into hard lumps, which means moisture has got in.
Mould or a musty smell in a jar that got damp — the only real safety issue.
tips: Buy whole seed and grind small amounts; the difference is dramatic.
Toast the seed in a dry pan for a minute before grinding.
Never shake ground cumin straight from the jar over a steaming pan.
If the jar smells of nothing, replace it — no amount of extra spoonfuls will fix it.

faq.q: How long does ground cumin keep?
faq.a: 3–4 years from purchase in an airtight jar in a cool, dark cupboard, opened or unopened.
No. Ground spices fade rather than spoil, so an old jar is weak, not unsafe. Only a damp jar that has grown mould should be thrown out.

faq.q: How can you tell if cumin is still good?
faq.a: Warm a pinch in your palm and smell it. If nothing rises off it, it has nothing left to give the dish.

zh.name: 孜然粉
zh.summary: 孜然粉自購買日起，放在陰涼避光的櫥櫃可放 3～4 年，開封與否都一樣。一罐放了一年半的孜然並不危險——它只是比以前弱了。這個數字是風味的窗口，不是安全的上限。
zh.pantry: 氣密罐、陰涼、避光、遠離爐台的蒸氣，自購買日起 3～4 年。乾燥研磨的孜然含水量遠遠不足以讓任何東西生長，所以沒有東西在腐敗；只是那些芳香精油一直在離開，而溫度和光線會讓它跑得快一點。請用聞的而不是看日期：倒一點在手心，用拇指搓熱，再聞。新鮮的孜然是直接而帶土香的；退掉的那罐只剩灰塵味。整粒的香氣撐得比粉久；而下鍋前用乾鍋烘一分鐘再磨，連普通的孜然都會變得有模有樣。
zh.fridge: 冰箱對孜然粉是個很差的選擇。研磨香料會吸濕，冰過的罐子每次在溫暖廚房打開，水氣就落在粉上；受潮的孜然會結塊，也可能發霉。密封罐放在遠離爐具的櫥櫃，才是它該待的地方。
zh.freezer: 冷凍同樣沒有期限數據，而結露問題在冷凍庫只會更嚴重。真正有用的一步，是改買整粒孜然——它因為暴露的表面少而比粉耐放——下鍋前再烘香現磨。那給你的東西，比任何低溫保存都多。
zh.thawing: 不適用——孜然粉是乾燥的櫥櫃香料，不應冷凍。
spoilage: 在手心搓熱一小撮，完全聞不到味道。
只剩灰塵般的平板氣味，而不是溫暖的土香。
結成硬塊，代表水氣跑進去了。
受潮的罐子長霉或有霉味——這是唯一真正的安全問題。
tips: 買整粒、少量現磨；差別非常明顯。
磨之前先用乾鍋烘一分鐘。
絕對不要拿著罐子在冒蒸氣的鍋子上方抖。
如果罐子聞起來什麼都沒有就換掉——加再多匙也補不回來。

faq.a: 氣密罐放陰涼避光的櫥櫃，自購買日起 3～4 年，開封與否都一樣。

faq.q: 放很久的孜然有危險嗎？
faq.a: 沒有。研磨香料是淡掉而不是腐敗，舊罐子只是味道弱。只有受潮長霉的才該丟。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷孜然還能不能用？
faq.a: 在手心搓熱一小撮聞聞看。如果什麼都沒有飄上來，它對這道菜也就沒什麼可以給了。
